scope: Topic 058 Ghẹ Hàm Ninh - food identity, trademark, eating practical and source-origin caveats.

topics.title: Ghẹ Hàm Ninh

claims.claim: A collective trademark for 'Ghẹ Hàm Ninh, Phú Quốc' was certified in 2022; local-government and related institutional reporting documents the certification and later use by authorized households.
In February 2025, the provincial Farmers' Association reported that collective-mark signage was handed to 14 households directly involved in harvesting, catching and trading Ghẹ Hàm Ninh.

The existence of an authorized collective mark means Open Phu Quoc should not assume every crab sold by a restaurant in Hàm Ninh is automatically collective-mark Ghẹ Hàm Ninh or was caught locally. Source/origin must be verified separately.
Vietnam's official tourism site describes Ghẹ Hàm Ninh as a small rosy-speckled flower crab associated with Hàm Ninh and commonly enjoyed boiled with lime-pepper salt.

Current destination content describes Hàm Ninh seafood as primarily nearshore catch with short transport time. This supports a local-fishing context but does not establish origin for every restaurant's inventory.
Recent tourism pages publish indicative crab prices, but price is highly volatile by size, sex, supply and venue. No single current price is locked for Open Phu Quoc yet.
Ghẹ is a crustacean shellfish, so crustacean shellfish must be flagged as a major allergen in food content.
